text: Suncogs are Mechanical collectible items in . They can be gathered from the old machines in the Kingdom of Torna, the old machine east of the Auresco, Main Gate Skip Travel point in Auresco, the old machine in the center of Peln, Pilgrim's Springland in the Dannagh Region, and the large old machine on the southeast edge of the Verdant Fairylands in the Dannagh Region.
Sweet Nothings are a Key Item in . They can be crafted by Lora and is required to complete the quest Helping the Helper.

Supreme Sport Glasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. They are an upgraded version of the Redesigned Sport Glasses and share their appearance with them.
Supreme Round Sunglasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.
Supreme Glasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.

Survee Antols (Japanese: , Seruwī Antoru) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Antol family and can be found at level 28 - 34 at The Great Breaksand in the Dannagh Region of the Kingdom of Torna. They may emerge from Knoober Pods. Four Survee Antols must be defeated to unlock Mythra's level 3 Terminal Flash.
Stustu is a DLC NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found in the Heat Storage of the Old Factory in the Empire of Mor Ardain where she must be looked for during the DLC Quest Industrial Sort of Tour.
Swirling Dragon (Japanese: , karyū) is Brighid's Level III Blade Special in . Swirling Dragon is also Brighid's Special Art during Merc Assault missions in the .
Sword Strike (Japanese: , Sōdosutoraiku) is Hugo's Switch Art in .
Supreme Swimsuit Tops are Casual Wear torso armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.
Supreme Swimmer's Band Ls are Casual Wear left arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.
Supreme Swimmer's Band Rs are Casual Wear right arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.

Subzero Steels (Japanese: , Kōrudo Suchīru, Cold Steel) are collectables in . They can be found on the Bionis' Shoulder. According to the description, they are bars of steel that chills to the bone, even affecting short-term memory.

Supplant the Noble Brogs (Japanese: , Nōburu Guroggu no Tōbatsu) is a quest in . It can be received once Laennar's Worries from Laennar is accepted at Companions' Cape on Bionis' Shoulder, or later at Agni's Birthplace.

Swirly Slashes (Japanese: , Kurukuru Surasshu) are collectables in . They can be found on the Bionis' Shoulder. According to the description, they are stones Nene named as she skimmed one across the water, and it never stopped.

Sweetest Debt (Japanese: , Kari wa Puririmu de Kansai) is a quest in . It can be received from Arara at the Grand Arch in Gran Dell on the Bionis' Shoulder. To receive this quest Melia must be the party lead.

Stubborn Minds (Japanese: , Iji) is a quest in . It can be received from Winnie at the Gran Dell Approach on the Bionis' Shoulder after Rival Hearts has been completed and the Monado Replica EX+ has been acquired.
The Sweet Cherry is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. It is found along the banks of the Tranquil Tarn, and is required for Sweetest Debt given by Arara.
Sun Visors are Mechonis goggles in . They can be obtained as rewards after clearing the Time Attack challenge Third Wheel. They can only be worn by Fiora.

Supreme Sunglasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. They are an upgraded version of the Bargain Sunglasses and share their appearance with them.
Sword Blossom (Japanese: , Sōdoburossamu) is Addam's Level I Special in . As with Addam's other specials, the element of Sword Blossom is determined by the Greatsword he has equipped.
Sweet Emotion (Japanese: ) is Kora's Level IV Blade Special in .
Swordmarch (Japanese: , Taiken, lit: The Great Sword) is a Region of Aionios in .
Swordfighter (Japanese: , Sōdofaitā) is a Kevesi Attacker class in .
Swimming Merfreys are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Merfrey family, and can be found at level 62-63 near Daedal Isle and in Patulia Bay in Erythia Sea.
Supreme Blants are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Blant family, and can be found at level 55-59 in Farlaine Underpass in Erythia Sea. __TOC__

Sword Ignas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at level 19 on Ribbi Flats, level 42-43 on Elaice Highway, and at level 99 in Rebellion Cave at Erythia Sea.
Sudden Impact (Japanese: , Sadon'inpakuto) is a Battle Art in . It is one of Lanz's Ouroboros arts.

Supplies in the Wind is a Standard Quest in . It can be received from Pollux in Yzana Plains.

Sundappled Floria (Japanese: , Komorebi no Furōria) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Garaffa family, and can be found at level 71 at N'ohm Wetlands in Great Sword's Base. The Electric Skin Art can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Strong Foot Wraps are Accessories in and . In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Cryoconite Laurel.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Strung Ambers are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Lambda Commissary.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Swimmer's Chemises are Accessories in and . They can obtained by completing Carrie's Collectopaedia Card, or buying it from Hilltop Caravan. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Cryoconite Laurel.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Sturdy Anklets are Accessories in and . The legendary variant can be obtained from Spectral Rémy. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Sworn Protector Hector.
Sturc Gully Gate (Japanese: , Zara Kyōkoku-mon) is a Landmark in . It is located at the Great Sword's Base. It connects to the Syra Hovering Reefs in the Keves Castle Region.
Supply Storage #1 (Japanese: , Daiichi Busshi Hokanshitsu) is a Rest Spot in . It is located in the South Sector Passage in the Origin Interior.

Sycophantic Lilith (Japanese: , Tsuishō no Ririsu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 5 southwest of the Colony 9 Front Gate in Yzana Plains. The Hard Dig Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it. It can drop Dextrous Bunnit Tail and Bunnit Meat when defeated.
Supply Storage #2 (Japanese: , Daini Busshi Hokanshitsu) is a Landmark in , located in the Origin Interior.
Survivors (Japanese: , Ikiyuku Monotachi) is a Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Juniper.
Surge Circuits are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. They can also be produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Sundialflowers are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. It can also be purchased from Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan, or produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Suite Peas are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Battlescar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Submit Gogols are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 52-53 on Elaice Highway.

The Swaroog Rhana is a Quest Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Rhana family, and is fought at level 58 in the Low Maktha Wildwood during The Ultimate Vessel. It drops an Origin Metal upon defeat.

The Sweet Plambus is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Plambus family, and is fought at level 37 near the Old Way Camp at the Old Cliffside Way during A More Balanced Recipe. It drops an Armored Plambus Wing and the Fermenting Bug Juices.
Sunny Aloes are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Sweetcaps are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Stringy-Wingy Veggie Leclatis are Meal items in . They can be cooked by Manana at Rest Spots. 1 Silver Nopon Coin can be used to cook this meal instead of the necessary ingredients. It can be unlocked by purchasing the Meat 'n' Veg Leclati from the Gamma Canteen for the first time.
Sword Merignas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Merigna family, and can be found at level 46 and 72 in Erythia Sea.
Summon Element is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Royal Summoner class. It becomes a usable Master Art upon unlocking the class.
Svinne Cavity (Japanese: , Shavīne Kūdō) is a Location in , located on Yzana Plains in the Aetia Region.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Survivor Kneeguards are Accessories in and . The common variant can be purchased from the Sandbar Caravan. The legendary variant can be obtained from Hardshelled Admory. In , the legendary variant can be obtained from Peacebringer Divalo.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Survival Belts are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be dropped by Kilocorn Grandeps or Creeping Hameel.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Strung Jades are Accessories in . The common variant can be purchased from the Korresia's Shop.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Strung Lapis Lazulis are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be purchased from the Prize X-change Blue.
Sweetless Brogs are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 78-79 east of Viliera Hill in Millick Meadows.

Sword of Valor (Japanese: , Bureibusōdo, "Brave Sword") is a Talent Art in . It is the Talent Art of the Yumsmith class. The Art inflicts the Damage Link debuff on the targeted enemy, which damages enemies nearby the debuffed enemy should they be damaged further. When Riku & Manana use this Talent Art, it is called Sharpest Tool (Japanese: ).
Sunny-Style Fish Pies are Meal items in . They can be purchased from the Colony Mu Canteen. Purchasing it for the first time unlocks the Creamy-Dreamy Fish Pie recipe for Manana's Menu.
Sunny's Sampler Set is a DLC Key Item in . It can be obtained from Sunny during the DLC Quest Going Full HD. It can be given to Totoma to upgrade the HD Ether Cylinder+ to Ver. 2.0.
Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan is a DLC Shop in . It is run by Sumomo and can be found at the Namba Mound Camp in the Dannagh Desert after the Hero Quest Champion of the Nopon is completed.

Sumomo is a NPC in . She is a Nopon from the Nopon Caravans who is found at the Namba Mound Camp in the Dannagh Desert after the DLC Quest Champion of the Nopon has been completed. Sumomo runs a shop called Sunny & Cheerio's Caravan.
Superstorm (Japanese: , Tenpesuto Lit. "Tempest") is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Full Metal Jaguar class.

Sturm und Drang (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Dragon's Snarl that can only be used by Cammuravi. He moves back lighting his lance on fire then throws it at the enemy while also taking damage himself.
Suprise Beat is a Battle Art in . It is an art that can only be used by Valdi.
Sweet Breeze (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is a variant of Autumn Rain that can only be used by Miyabi.

Surprise Beat (Japanese: , Sapuraizubīto) is a Battle Art in exclusive to Valdi. He turns and does a hard stomp. The Art inflicts the Attack Down debuff, in addition to having boosted damage against Machine-type enemies.

Sumo Press (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Indiscreet Gombaba while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Sword Bind is a Status Effect in . It only affects Attackers and prevents them from taking any actions during the effect. The debuff is only inflicted by Moebius H whenever she uses the Art "Moebius Dominion: Attackers", and cannot be inflicted by the player's party.
Supreme Turtlenecks are Casual Wear torso armor in . They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries and are apart of the Custom Diving armor range.

The Sullied Temple of Abitalia (Japanese: , Kesareta Shinden Abitaria Ikō) is a location in , located south of the Ferronis Crater on the Aurora Shelf. It is home to several different Fogbeasts and a Fog Rift. The Unique Monsters Fogtrawler Tallstuff and Gotthard, the Ethereal can be found here as well.
|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Sunlight Rings are Accessories in . The legendary variant can be acquired from Fogtrawler Tallstuff.
Sword of Liberation (, Kaihō no ken) is Shulk & Rex's Chain Art in .

Surrogate Fitzpatrick (Japanese: , Karioya no Furikamui) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Vollgull family, and can be found at level 41 on Raguel Bridge on the The Ragmos Desolation. He only appears when the party approaches the 3 Vollgull Eggs on the bridge.

Sworn Protector Hector (Japanese: , Shugo no Kongou) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 32 at the Waterlogged Daksha Shrine on the The Ragmos Desolation.
Swimswam's Amulet - Gold is a Key Item in . It is received from Bobobi during Nopon Medals Needed.
Swimswam's Amulet - Silver is a Key Item in . It is received from Bobobi during Nopon Medals Needed.

Sun-Dappled Glade is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda and Mariam Abounnasr. It is track seven of disc three from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track seven of disc fourteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * During the flashback where Riku presents Lucky Seven to Noah. * After the cooking contest concludes during Happiness.

Suffocating Reverberation is a track in and , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track seven of disc two from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track seven of disc thirteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during dire and shocking moments in various cutscenes.

Suspicion is a track in and , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track six of disc three from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track six of disc fourteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * During the Chapter 2 flashback of when Garvel interrupts Noah's training. * N, X, Y, and Z watching the party from the Amphitheater as the party travels through Rae-Bel Tableland. * When Ethel and Bolearis meet with N and the Queen of Keves, and when Ethel provides Bolearis with the plans of Keves Castle. * Ethel and Cammuravi's conversation in Keves Castle. * When the party discovers the new incarnation of Ethel in Keves Castle. * T
Stunned Swallow (Japanese: , Rōen, "Hazy Swallow") is a Battle Art in . It is one of Jin's arts as a temporary party member during Chapter 8 and during the Challenge Battle Titan Battleship Assault.
Superdreadnought Xern (Japanese: , Chōdokyū Yōsai-gata Zerun) is a Tyrant in . It is a Xern machine. It can be found at level 59 above the Ravaged Vargo in Volitaris.
Surgical Strike Pugilith (Japanese: , Tekisenkō Senryoku Haigeki-gata Berudero) is a Tyrant in . It is a Pugilith machine. It can be found at level 53 in the Ochus Corridor in Volitaris.
Sylvalian Tree Saps are two Important Items in . They can be found on the east shore of Lake Ciel in Sylvalum. They must be collected during New Skell on the Block.
The Succulent Suid Shoulder is an Important Item in . It is acquired from the Meaty Suid near Primordia's Sayram Lake during One Big Happy Family.
Support Familivs are Story Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Familiv family, and can be found at level 59 inside the Tower of Eternity on Volitaris after being summoned by Void.
The Summoning Goggles are an Important Item in . It is collected from Yin'tonam in the Industrial District at the beginning of Lone Survivors.
Stunner is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a character stuns an enemy and prevents them from moving.
Stuffed Lobster is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found around New Los Angeles during Rise of the Blood Lobster, 99 of them must be recovered to complete this mission.
The Survival Torso is a BLADE torso armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

Tephra Cave (Japanese: , Tefura Dōkutsu; English dub: ) is a large, cavernous area in . The cave is located inside the Bionis' right leg spanning from the right calf to its kneecap. It must be navigated at least twice throughout the game, once to reach the Cylinder Hangar and once to reach Bionis' Leg. It is first reached via the Tephra Cave Entrance at Colony 9. Tephra Cave is the first area where Ether Crystals can be mined.
The Tephra Cave Collection is a portion of the Collectopaedia in .

Sylviane (Japanese: , Suruwa) is a Homs in . She can be found just south of the Ether Light, in front of the ether lamp stall, in the Commercial District of Colony 9. She is in league with King Squeeze to make her boyfriend Leopold spend all his money on her, so that King Squeeze can take his house as payment for his loan and retire.

Tephra Lizards (Japanese: , Tefura Rizado) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Lizard family, and can be found at level 8-9 in Vilia Lake in Tephra Cave. Defeating five of them is required to complete the quest Jackson's Awakening given by Jackson in Colony 6.

Tati (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in . He can be found in the Nopon Kitchen in Frontier Village. Tati can be heard coughing before completing Strange Noises from Below. He is a musician as well as a chef and he can be heard singing after the series of quests he gives.
The Tank Guarder (Japanese: , Tankugādā) is a weapon in . It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.

Talonyth (Japanese: , Tatedonasu) is a High Entia in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found south of the Main Entrance to Alcamoth, next to the second fountain passed. After moving to Colony 6, he manages the restaurant north of Reconstruction HQ. If he was not recruited before the events at the Mechonis Core, he can be found at the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg, in front of the pond. He is a really popular chef who desires for a taste of competition and gets into a rivalry with Hoko when his food starts to improve.

Territorial Rotbart (Japanese: , Nawabari Barubarossa, lit. Territorial Barbarossa) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 81 on the Gaur Plain between Jabos Rock Rest Area and Rho Oasis, on the Bionis' Leg. It must be defeated to complete the Colony 6 quest Homs Determination, given by Perrine if she moves to Colony 6. It can also drop the Gogol Horns required for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction. It deals topple spike damage and gains a Crazed aura below 30% health. Territorial Rotbart is the third highest leveled enemy on Bionis' Leg after Armoured Rockwell, a Torta at level 82, and Immovable Gonzalez, another Gogol at level
Teelan (Japanese: , Teto) is a half-Homs High Entia in . In , he is a major supporting character.

Talia (Japanese: , Taria) is a High Entia NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found southwest of the Imperial Palace in Alcamoth during the night. During Talia's Research or Investigating Satorl, Talia can be found anytime at the Place of Judgement in Satorl Marsh. After the events at the Mechonis Core, she can be found at Ether Plant in Eryth Sea during the night. She is a researcher looking into the War God Statue and the origins behind the faith to it.

Tasty Sausages (Japanese: , Amaama Win'na) are collectables in . They can be found in the High Entia Tomb. According to their description, Riki was munching on one when he named them and they are sweet golden tubelike things.

Tap Tap Taps (Japanese: , Ratatatarattatta) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Bionis' Interior. According to their description, Riki danced as he named them and they can come in handy at a dance.

Tail Antennae (Japanese: , Tēru Antena) are collectables in . They can be found in Galahad Fortress and Colony 6. According to their description, they are cute like a cat's tail and they have distinctive rigid forms.

The Tephra Cave Entrance (Japanese: , Tefura Dōkutsu Iriguchi) is a landmark in . It is located in Colony 9, and leads to Tephra Cave. The landmark is along the western cliffs of Colony 9. Though there are no enemies at the Tephra Cave Entrance, there are some Wood Bunnits and Ridge Antols a little ways south-east. "Enduring Friendship" (a Heart-to-Heart between Shulk and Reyn) is located here, as well as a Defence Force soldier who will give the party quests for Tephra Cave.
Taurus Helms (Japanese: , Taurosu Herumu) are heavy head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are designed after old Machina gear.
Taurus Plates are heavy torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are based off of old Machina gear. They can be dropped by the Wrathful Orobas.
Taurus Arms are heavy arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are based off of old Machina gear.
Taurus Cuisses are heavy legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Offensive/LYRICs. They are based on old Machina gear.
Taurus Greaves are heavy feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by the Commander Oracion.

Teneb Vangs (Japanese: , Tenebu Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at level 32 in the Hode Lair in Makna Forest at night. They can also be found in the cave connecting to the Divine Sanctuary. They can drop the Delicious Vang Tails needed for one route of Popularity Premonition.

The Tatty Armor is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Finding it is one of the objectives of Mementos of a Lost Son. It is located in Tephra Cave, near where three dead merchants are found. This ruined armor belonged to Cheryl's son.

Tephra Cavern (Japanese: , Tefura Daikūdō) is a location in . It is located in the center of Tephra Cave, at roughly the same place as the Spring of Grief. It is the location of the Solid Konev. There is a pathway that is blocked, but laters open up after the events at the Mechonis Core, revealing the second part of Tephra Cave.

Telethia Vol'aren (Japanese: , Tereshia no Borario) is quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Licorne-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 90 near the Fountain of Hope in Alcamoth during A Memento of Daddy, right after the Family Picture is obtained. It is Vol'aren after turning into a Telethia.

The Terminal Trachea (Japanese: , Tainai Shūmatsu Kikan-ji) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of the Bionis' Interior. It is the entrance into the Bionis' Interior from Satorl Marsh, the first time the party visits the area. It leads north to the Third Lung, where the sole NPC in the entire area, a Nopon, is found.

The Telethia Arielle (Japanese: , Tereshia no Arietta) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Phoenix-type member of the Telethia family, encountered at level 86 near the Fountain of Eternity in Alcamoth during The Only Thing I Can Do or I Will Never Forget You. It used to be Arielle, who turned into a Telethia after the Mechonis Core event due to her being a pureblooded High Entia. Having previously been one of Vidian's friends, it saves her during the incident in Alcamoth. In the quest, Vidian asks the party to defeat the Telethia so that her friend's suffering will end. In addition to her normal drops, Telethia Arielle always drops Arielle's Ring.

The Telethia Lesunia (Japanese: , Tereshia no Ruīze) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Phoenix-type member of the Telethia family, encountered at level 86 near Melfica Road in Alcamoth during The Only Thing I Can Do or I Will Never Forget You. It used to be Lesunia, who turned into a Telethia after the Mechonis Core event due to her being a pureblooded High Entia. Having previously been one of Vidian's friends, it saves her during the incident in Alcamoth. In the quest, Vidian asks the party to defeat the Telethia so that her friend's suffering will end. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Lesunia always drops an Affection Seal Half.
Tephra Path (Japanese: , Tefura-dōri) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of Tephra Cave. It is the path that leads into Tephra Cave.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Talia's Research (Japanese: , Taria no Kenkyū) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Talia in Alcamoth after A Necessary Upgrade is completed. This quest and the Investigating Satorl Eryth Sea quest are mutually exclusive. By completing either this quest or Investigating Satorl, the party will have access to the next quest, Ancient High Entia Mystery, that will unlock Melia's fifth skill branch.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Teaching Materials (Japanese: , Kyōzai no Zairyō wo Atsumete) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Mir'leiz southwest of the Imperial Palace, near the entrance, in Alcamoth, from 06:00 to 18:00. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

Syrath Lighthouse (Japanese: , Shiuerāto Tōdai) is a landmark in . It is located on Hovering Reef 4 in Eryth Sea. A shop is located on top of the lighthouse, as is a Heart-to-Heart - "Riki Have Question". The shop is manned by a male High Entia. A quest at this location unlocks Melia's fourth skill branch, Reticence.
Tatty Bunniv Wood is a rare material in . It can be dropped by Willow Bunnivs, or traded for.
Telethia Light Wings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only dropped by two types of Telethia in the Bionis' Interior.

Terrain Defence (Japanese: , Chikei Bōgyo) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that reduces damage taken from hazardous environments, including poisonous swamps, hot lava, and pools of ether. Such terrain normally inflicts damage equal to 20% of a character's maximum HP at regular intervals, usually every two seconds. Physical or Ether Defence do not reduce damage from hazardous terrain. __TOC__

Tension Swing (Japanese: , Tenshon Hendō) is a Gem in that reduces the Tension range, making it easier to gain or lose tension. This can be useful for arts such as Happy Happy and Final Cross, which require high tension to activate. __TOC__

Talent Boost (Japanese: , Tarento Būsuto) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that increases Talent Gauge gain from, but halves the damage dealt by auto-attacks. The effects of this gem apply even for Melia and Sharla, whose Talent Gauges are not normally filled by auto-attacks. It is inadvisable to equip it on Sharla, as it would cause her weapon to overheat sooner. __TOC__

Temporal Gawain (Japanese: , Seisō no Gawein) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Faced Mechon, and can be found at level 65 in the Central Factory. It is found inside the Control Tower, after opening the hangar's doors, along with some Mass-Produced Faces. It has a Topple damage counter spike.
Tempest Kick (Japanese: , Fūjin Senkyaku) is one of Dunban's Ether arts in . If used after Gale Slash, it removes one buff from the target and fills the Party Gauge by 20%.

Terra Orlugas (Japanese: , Terara Oruga) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Orluga family, and can be found at level 31 outside the Frontier Village Entrance. Defeating three of them is required to complete Frontier Village's quest Monster Quest 2 - Part 1. They can drop the Orluga Grass Skirts required for Alcamoth's Material Quest 2.

Tasty Ansel Wings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Ansels in Makna Forest and traded for in Frontier Village. According to their description, the taste of these miracle foods change seven times in the mouth. Two are needed for Heropon's Spirit.

Taos (Japanese: , Taōsu) is a family of avian enemies in the . They come in blue and orange varieties, and undergo no appearance changes between games, except in and where Taos only come in an orange species and Tokilos in a close blue exclusive species.

The Tear of the Sky is a Key Item in . It can be found on the Distant Fingertip on the Fallen Arm, only during a thunderstorm. Obtaining it for Zarkort is the objective of For My Loved One.... Then during To My Loved One..., Zarkort gives the item to the party and asks to offer it to Bozatrox.
Tantrum (Japanese: , Yatchau mo) is one of Riki's physical arts in . It damages enemies ahead of Riki with a three hit combo. The final hit may inflict Break on the enemies.

Test Pit 4 (Japanese: , Chika Kōdō Dai 4 Shikutsu-ba) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor in the Ether Mine, and can be found by taking the right path from the Central Terminal. It is inhabited by Colony Upas, Colony Lizards, and the Vengeful Daulton. A vast Ice Ether Crystal deposit containing Ether Def Up II and Blaze Defence II crystals can be found near here. The rank of these crystals increases during Colony 6 Reconstruction when Colony 6's Nature level is increased to level 3 and above.
Tarifa Hodes are enemies in . They are members of the Hode family, and can be found at level 35 at the Hode Refuge at Eryth Sea.

Synchronised Gaheris (Japanese: , Rensō no Gaherisu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found in the Central Factory, between the stacks of containers east of the Central Tower Lift and north-northwest of the Central Warehouse Lift.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in Tephra Cave.

Telethia Lecrough (Japanese: , Tereshia no Rokuro) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Phoenix-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 87 in the Great Hall in Alcamoth during A Release From Duty and is one of four unique Telethia that must be defeated in Alcamoth to complete the quest. The other three are Telethia Galdo, Telethia Kaelin, and Telethia Donnis. It is the Telethia form of Lecrough. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Lecrough drops an Armour Shard.

The Telethia Galdo (Japanese: , Tereshia no Gāda) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Phoenix-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 88 in the Imperial Villa in Alcamoth during A Release From Duty and is one of four unique Telethia which must be defeated in Alcamoth to complete the quest. The other three are Telethia Lecrough, Telethia Kaelin, and Telethia Donnis. It is the Telethia form of Galdo. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Galdo always drops an Armour Shard.

Telethia Kaelin (Japanese: , Tereshia no Kaito) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Drakos-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 89 on the Sky Terrace in Alcamoth during A Release From Duty. It is the Telethia form of Kaelin, and is one of four unique Telethia which must be defeated in Alcamoth to complete the quest. The other three are Telethia Lecrough, Telethia Galdo, and Telethia Donnis. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Kaelin always drops an Armour Shard.

Telethia Donnis (Japanese: , Tereshia no Dona) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a Licorne-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 91 in the Audience Chamber in Alcamoth during A Release From Duty and is one of four unique Telethia in Alcamoth which must be defeated to complete the quest. The other three are Telethia Lecrough, Telethia Galdo, and Telethia Kaelin. It is the Telethia form of Donnis. In addition to its normal drops, Telethia Donnis always drops an Armour Shard.

In and , a character's Talent Gauge is a measure of how close a character is to being able to use their Talent Art, or how close they are to other side effects that come from a full Talent Gauge. Unlike normal arts, Talent Arts have no cooldown, and will not refill over time, and thus a character must manually refill their Talent Gauge on their own.

The Tephra Drop is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is needed for Romantic Notions of a Girl and Romantic Notions of a Boy. There is only one Tephra Drop available, so the choice must be made of which quest to complete. The Tephra Drop can be found in Tephra Cave at night near the Spring of Grief, but only while at least one of the Romantic Notions quests is active.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Telethia Investigation 1 (Japanese: , Tereshia Chōsa Sono 1) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from the Strategic Intel Terminal at the Central Tower in Agniratha. All the quests in Agniratha must be completed in order to get the Cloister Key from the Capital Control Terminal to enter the Seven Sage Cloister.

This quest will expire after the events at the Mechonis Core. Telethia Investigation 2 (Japanese: , Tereshia Chōsa Sono 2) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from the Strategic Intel Terminal at the Central Tower in Agniratha. All the quests in Agniratha must be completed in order to get the Cloister Key from the Capital Control Terminal to enter the Seven Sage Cloister.

The Terminal Nerve Tower (Japanese: , Shūmatsu Shinkei Tawā) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of the Bionis' Interior, southwest of the Venous Plexus. A Heart-to-Heart - "Kind Words" - is located here. The Ghostly Mahatos can be found here, in addition to an Ether Crystal deposit containing Ether Def Up V and Arts Stealth V crystals.

The Terminal Vein (Japanese: , Mattan Jōmyaku) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Interior, north of the Pars Sympathica Tower. An Ether Crystal deposit containing Muscle Up V and Attack Plus V crystals can be found here.

Test Pit 3 (Japanese: , Chika Kōdō Dai 3 Shikutsu-ba) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine, west of Test Pit 1. A Rock and Junk Krabble inhabit the Test Pit itself, while a Mechon M32X patrols nearby. A Wind Ether Crystal deposit containing Agility Up II and Agility Down II crystals can be found near here. The rank of these crystals increases during Colony 6 Reconstruction when Colony 6's Nature level is increased to level 3 and above.

Test Pit 1 (Japanese: , Chika Kōdō Dai 1 Shikutsu-ba) is a location in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine, and is found by entering the mine from the Drainage Control Room, then heading left at the first fork in the tunnels. A lone M42 Scout Unit patrols the area. North of Test Pit 1 is an Earth Ether Crystal deposit containing Muscle Up II and Bleed Defence II crystals. The rank of these crystals increases during Colony 6 Reconstruction when Colony 6's Nature level is increased to level 3 and above.
Telethia Tomes are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from the Ghostly Mahatos and Gigas Telethia in Bionis' Interior. Telethia Tomes are not otherwise available.
Telethia Membranes are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by the Furious Jozan or be traded for with Ricoth.
Telethia Letters are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by the Vivid Anstan and Licorne Telethia.
Tasty Vang Feathers are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Sierra Vangs.
Telethia Feathers are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are not dropped by any enemies, but can be traded for with Leku.
Telethia Tear Jewels are rare materials designed for Xenoblade Chronicles. For unknown reasons they were cut from the game. It was most likely intended to have been dropped by Disciple Lorithia.

Telethia Pouches are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained by trading with Tuzu in Frontier Village. Telethia Pouches are otherwise not available. According to their description, they are bags full of ether which are poisonous to the body.

Telethia Compasses are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained by trading with Caul in Alcamoth. Telethia Compasses are otherwise not available. According to their description, they are compasses that predict the weather eight hours ahead and are one-hundred percent accurate.

Tatsu (Japanese: ; English dub: ) is a Nopon native to Mira in . He is met by Cross upon being freed from a vegetable containment unit in Chapter 3. After introductions, he accompanies Cross, Elma, Lin, and their companions for the rest of the game. Unlike Riki from , Tatsu is not a playable character. However, he is a major support character who assists the main cast on their journey. He automatically joins or leaves the party if Lin does the same.

Terebras (Japanese: , Rutoru) are otter-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They have long bodies with four short legs and a thick tapered tail, giving them a streamlined shape well-suited for swimming. Unlike otters, they have extremely large forward-facing ears that can be closed over their heads, for defense or added aqua-dynamics. They are much larger than real otters, though still small compared to most Miran indigens. They can be found in Primordia and Noctilum.

Tension (緊張) is an Event Track in and , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 8 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is an enigmatic, ominous theme that is heard during the cutscene when Juju sneaks out of the Refugee Camp in his buggy, and later when Miqol makes his request to the party to kill his son Egil. In , this song plays when the party first sees the rift in Alcamoth, when the party notices the rift having appeared outside of Alcamoth, and when the party considers the possibility of monsters on the Bionis' Shoulder becoming Fogbeasts.
The Syrath Lighthouse Shop is a shop in . It is located at the top of Syrath Lighthouse in Eryth Sea. A male High Entia mans the shop, which has a good selection of Unique weapons.
Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Tapenta) are tortoise-like insectoids in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They often are camouflaged as rocks. They can be found in Noctilum and Oblivia.
Tallpach Peak (Japanese: , Vangisu no Iwayama) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, west of North Janpath Plain and east of the Silent Mire.

Terrible Germivores (Japanese: , Terā Burōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Germivore family, and can be found at level 23 at Qing Long Glade, Dead Man's Ingress or near Great Nail in Noctilum. Defeating five of them is required during Germivores No More.

Telethia, the Endbringer (Japanese: , Shūen no Tereshia) is a Tyrant in . It is a form of the Telethia and is found in Noctilum, above the Divine Roost. At level 99, it is the highest level enemy in the Wii U version, and tied with Glossolalia, the Allochthon and Apocalypsis, the Sacrificant as the highest level enemy in the , yet it is non-aggressive and will not attack the party first. The battle with Telethia, the Endbringer begins in the air, but Telethia, the Endbringer will descend onto the ground when it has between 65% and 70% HP. It will later return to the sky once its HP has been reduced to between 25% and 30%. If it is in the middle of descending or ascending, it is immune to all
Talon Rock Second Terrane (Japanese: , Kagizumeiwa no Daini Dansōbu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, northwest of Sayram Northeast Plain.
Tharros Scirpos (Japanese: , Tarosu Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Scirpos and can be found at level 37-40 around FN Site 217 in Noctilum.

The Targeter Zigs (Japanese: , Tāgetto Jigu) are three story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Zig machines and can found at level 16 at various locations in Oblivia during Chapter 5. One can be found to the south of Cliffside Camp, guarded by Prone Purgers and a Marnuck Vanguard. Another is located in Mesa Fortress, guarded by Dagger Puges and a Prone Damned. The third is located in a dead end near the southern end of the Stoyanov Trail, guarded by a Sword Pugilith. The party is tasked by the Ma-non to defeat the Targeter Zigs to show that they are not affiliated with the Ganglion.

That's In-Credible! (Japanese: , Itsuwari naki Shinshindō) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Tutura in front of BLADE Tower in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. It is one of three options for completing Proficiency Exam 8, but can be completed before receiving that mission.
Tellurium Oc-servs (Japanese: , Teruru Me-Tsuu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Oc-serv machines, and can be found at level 30 guarding the entrance to Sylvalum from Seabird's Beak.

The Tainted Caro (Japanese: , Puraedo Nokkusu) are three Story Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Tainted group as Caro variants infected by a virus. They are fought near Millstone Ridge in Noctilum at level 20 during Chapter 6, after retrieving the alien mech.

Tectonic Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Kurasuto Tapenta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Tectinsula family, and can be found at level 38-40 on the north side of the river near Balance Rock in Oblivia.
Talon Knight Qmoevas (Japanese: , Kurōnaito Kumūba) are Story Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 30 Qmoevas, and can be found in NLA's Commercial District during Chapter 8.
Territorial Sylooth (Japanese: , Tāfu Shirūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Sylooth family, and can be found at level 60 on Delusians South Summit in Sylvalum.
Talon Rock Third Terrane (Japanese: , Kagizumeiwa no Daisan Dansōbu) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, west of Talon Rock Second Terrane.
Tersquals (Japanese: , Rakenma) are aquatic quadrupedal reptilian-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are similar to Diluses.
Tauler is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found near the Arms Manufacturers terminal on Armory Alley in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles. He is a BLADE personnel.

T'phnom Shelf (Japanese: , To-Funomu Danchi) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, southeast of the O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins, southwest of the Boxtrap Checkpoint and northeast of Sunset Falls and the Kitsune Stronghold. The FN Site 511 is located here, and Ge Jewhe can be found here during Until the End.
T'phnom Shelf BC (Japanese: , To-Funomu Danchi BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Cauldros, on the T'phnom Shelf.
Ternion Fork BC (Japanese: , Mitsumata no Kiro BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp located in Cauldros, at the Ternion Fork.

T-Ray Lights (Japanese: , Toransuraito) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are can be found in southeastern Primordia, from East Gate Plain outside New Los Angeles to the Seaswept Base and South Janpath Plain. Four of them are needed for the Basic Mission Xenotech Research.
Thalluses (Japanese: , Arudare) are insect-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They look like big stick insects, relatively similar to Vivohasts. They can be found in Noctilum and Oblivia.

Terbium Petramands (Japanese: , Terubiumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family, and can be found at level 45-46 in the lava at Sunset Falls in Cauldros. Four of them must be defeated during Petramand Patrol.
Tenacious Moths (Japanese: , Jichuuga) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular in Divine Roost.

Taoman Acids (Japanese: , Taomana no San) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum, particularly on Seabird's Beak. Five of these must be gathered in the mission What's a Taoman?.

Taut Leathers are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be dropped by various indigens, including Terebras, Vespers in Primordia, and Caro in Cauldros. Five are needed for Setting Forth.

Tengu's Playground (Japanese: , Tengu no Asobiba) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a series of raised platforms and islets located in Cauldros, southeast of Sunset Falls and northwest of Kitsune Stronghold. It forms a path between the two.

Ternion Fork (Japanese: , Mitsumata no Kiro) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a path junction located in Cauldros, directly south of the FN Site 508. Its three paths lead to the Adder Byroad, the Dragonbone Promontory and Sunset Falls. The Ternion Fork BC is located here.

Thaddaeus, the Ultramafic (, Kigan no Tadeāshu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Cinicula family. It can be found at level 42 east of Lake Ciel in Sylvalum. It emerges from the ground.

Terenty, the Blademaster (Japanese: , Kengō no Cherenchī) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ictus family. It can be found at level 72 southeast of Capital Wreckage in Cauldros.

Tempest Auravises (Japanese: , Tenpesuto Akuira) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Auravis family, and can be found at level 58-60 in Oblivia, southwest of FN Site 315 quite close to the Kintrees Scenic Viewpoint. Seven must be defeated to complete Plucking Auravises.

Tectonic Blattas (Japanese: , Kurasuto Buratta, Crust Blatta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 21-30 in Oblivia, southeast of FN Site 301 or north of FN Site 303 during the day.

Telethia Emeralds are intergalactic materials in . They are obtained once Telethia Plume is defeated. After the Nemesis dies, the player must exchange all Appendage Fragments they might be keeping. One of those fragments will be chosen randomly to be traded for Emeralds, while the others will be exchanged for 1 Reward Ticket each. Telethia Emeralds are used to craft the Supercivilization Attire, Elite Supercivilization Attire, Red Bunnyband, White Bunnyband, and all bunny suit Casual Wear.

Tainted Scintimures (Japanese: , Puraedo Torizumo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Tainted group as a black Scintimure variant infected by a virus. They can be found at level 21-30 in Noctilum's Dead Man's Gulch.

The Tainted (Japanese: , Puraedo, Praedo) are a special group of creatures in . There are three types of tainted enemies, all found in Noctilum, primarily in Dead Man's Gulch. In the Enemy Index, these enemies are not considered to be in the same category as other variants of their families, although resemble them exactly other than their dark purple coloration and glowing eyes.
TP Overdrive is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Astral Crusader at rank 10.
Synchrony is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Galactic Knight at rank 10. Cross, Alexa and Yelv can use this skill.
Talon Raptor Galdrs (Japanese: , Kurōraputā Garudora) are unused enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Galdr machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and would have been found at level 41-50 in Cauldros.

Talon Eagle Galdr (Japanese: , Kurōīguru Garudora) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Galdr machines, Ganglion's vehicles, and can be found at level 55 around the O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins and at level 60 in the Ganglion Antropolis in Cauldros. There is also a dormant level 53 Talon Eagle Galdr at the O'rrh Sim Watchtowers.
Tantalum Oc-servs (Japanese: , Tantaru Me-Tsuu) are unused enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Oc-serv machines, and would have been found at level 41-50 in Cauldros.

Tantalum Fal-swos (Japanese: , Tantaru Gi-suo) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Fal-swo machines, and can be found at level 41-50 in Primordia, notably at the Bedrock Hold and Bedrock Hold Approach.

Tellurium Fal-swos (Japanese: , Teruru Gi-suo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Fal-swo machines, and can be found at level 41-50 above the Delusians North Summit in Sylvalum during the night.

Thallium Fal-swos (Japanese: , Tariu Gi-suo) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Fal-swo machines, and can be found at level 52 at Anvil Rock One and Anvil Rock Two, and at level 62 below Luxaar's Xern in Sylvalum.
Tactical Analyst is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Mastermind at rank 7. Cross and Mia can use this skill.
Tacit Censure is one of Hope's two Signature Arts in . Cross learns this art after completing the affinity mission A Present for Hope.

Tan'celeg (Japanese: , Tan'osaragu) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Although he first appears at the end of the Normal Mission Sun'celeg Rises, it is not possible to find him until after Circle of Life is completed at which point he can be found at the Outfitters Test Hangar in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles. He can be found later at the Biahno Water-Purification Plant in Primordia during the night.
Talon King Qmoevas (Japanese: , Kurōkingu Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 51-60 in Primordia, near FN Site 110 at night.

Talon Queen Qmoevas (Japanese: , Kurōkuīn Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 41 near FN Site 409 at Hilal Stronghold in Sylvalum, atop the nearby tower. They are dormant until approached.
Tasty Fish Bellies are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Balaenas or Cetos.
Ten'celeg is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Starboard of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles. He is the offspring of Sun'celeg.
TP Rebound is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It grants a low chance to receive 100 to 750 TP when taking damage.
Taunt: Barrier is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It gives a chance to activate Barrier when Taunted.
Taunt: Decoy is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It gives a chance to activate Decoy when Taunted.
Taunt: Supercharge is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It gives a chance to activate Supercharge when Taunted.
Tea for Two is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the segment directly east of Deliverance Park in the backyard of one of the nearby houses.

Teamwork is Lao's fourth Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It takes place in the morning in the Residential District, in the field north of the Cathedral and east of the Water Purification Plant.
TW772: Trinn (Japanese: , TW772: Tuin) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian.
Tempered Blade Modules are common materials in . They can be obtained from golden Shrads. Three are required for Lend an Ear. They are components in several Skell Superweapons.
Tectinsula Back Moss are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Tectinsulas. Two are required for the Basic Mission A Look at Lichen.
Terebra Oil Grease is a common material in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from yellow and blue Terebras. Three bottles of Terebra Oil Grease are needed for Skell Repair: Arm.
Talk of the Town is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a general store owner to obtain Mirage Scopes in Primordia.
Taming Tectinsulas is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Prospectors and the primary destination is Oblivia.

Team Corwin in Crisis is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Raleigh and the primary destination is the Administrative District. This mission leads into Unknown Assailant, though accepting it is not a prerequisite.

Tech Supply is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Tan'celeg and the primary destination is the Industrial District. Although not required to accept it, this mission leads into the Normal Mission Good Neighbors.
Tents by the Ton is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from BLADE HQ and the primary destination is Cauldros.
Tersqual Takedown is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Test Data Retrieval is a Basic Mission in and . It is a request from Candid & Credible and the primary destination is Noctilum.
Tectinsula Shells are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Tectinsulas.
Terebra Paw Stamps are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Terebras.
Terebra Water Grease is a common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from reddish Terebras.
T.P. Units are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Chantai's Galdr.
Thallus Crescent Hooks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Thalluses and as a reward item for completing the Squad Mission Botanical Confusion.
Tersqual Eel Kebabs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Tersquals. One is required for The Taste of Tersqual.

Tersqual Fire Pouches are unique materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from blue/red Tersquals in Cauldros. They are components in X, XV, and XX Thermal Res Up and SpecUp.THERM-RES augments.
Terebra A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black and purple terebra variant. It can be obtained from Shinhwa, the Sagacious in Noctilum.
Terebra B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a gray and brown terebra variant. It can be obtained from Archibolt, the Revolutionary in Primordia.
Tersqual A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue tersqual variant. It can be obtained from Agnes, the Divine-Scaled in Cauldros.
Tersqual B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a yellow tersqual variant. It can be obtained from Latis, the Bristle-Scaled in Sylvalum.
Thallus A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a dark thallus variant. It can be obtained from Pizelle, the Purple Lightning in Noctilum.
Thallus B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a white thallus variant. It can be obtained from Edgardo, the Carefree in Oblivia.
Tectinsula A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a jungle tectinsula variant. It can be obtained from Alfombra, the Transcendent in Noctilum.
Tectinsula B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a desert tectinsula variant. It can be obtained from Vittorio, the Battle-Scarred in Oblivia.
Telethia is a Holofigure in . It depicts a Telethia. It can be obtained from silver drops from Telethia, the Endbringer.

Tasty Lunch Box is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts the lunch box Moimoi requests to bring to Muimui during Bread and a Circus. It looks like the one Tatsu carries around. It is obtained as a reward for completing this Normal Mission.

Tasty Eggs is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.5, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting ten Potamuses. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Tank Tops are casual torso Armors made by Sakuraba Industries in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are available through several missions. All colors in this set have the same stats.

Territorial Aggression is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.17, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty-two Progens. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Taunting the Prone is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.18, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting five Dieter, the Epicures. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Take 'Em Down! is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.19, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting sixteen Coronids. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Terrain Damage Reducer is an armor Augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X that reduces the damage from hazardous terrain, such as the toxic waters of Vitriol Cesspool.
